faq.a: Saule is associated with the Kazakh form سَاوْلِه, whose core sense is saule; ray of light (kazakh).

faq.q: What is the origin of Saule?
faq.a: Saule is associated with Kazakh. Saule is Kazakh сәуле, meaning 'ray of light'. It is used as a female given name.
No — the underlying form is Kazakh, not Arabic.
Saule can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Kazakh-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Saule should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Säule is a Kazakh word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.a: In Urdu, Saule is rendered ساولے and carries the sense ساولے، روشنی کی کرن.

faq.q: What does Saule mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Saule is rendered ساوله and carries the sense ساوله، پرتو نور.
A romanized syllable approximation is sau-le. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Saule?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Saule, saule. Script forms are ساوله, ساولے, سَاوْلِه, सौले.

faq.q: Is Saule a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
